diagnostic_evidence.quote: While our architecture inherently ensures symplecticity, exact Hamiltonian conservation is not enforced, as the proposed architecture only guarantees an approximate Hamiltonian is enforced.

issues.failure_explanation: The introduction asserts the architecture 'ensur[es] energy conservation'. Symplectic maps preserve the symplectic form, not the value of a Hamiltonian; the paper itself concedes that exact Hamiltonian conservation is not enforced and adds only a soft penalty (eq:loss-ham), and the experiments report small Hamiltonian deviations rather than conservation. The prose thus claims a guarantee the formal content does not establish.

failure_location.quote: our architecture maintains the symplectic structure of the original system, ensuring energy conservation and numerical stability through nonlinear transformations

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Reword to 'approximate Hamiltonian preservation' as done in the abstract and results sections; a local editorial weakening with no mathematical loss.
issues.overall_effect: The advertised guarantee of energy conservation for the ROM is unsupported; only approximate Hamiltonian preservation (empirically small deviation) is established.
issues.title: Introduction claims the architecture ensures energy conservation
issues.why_classification: A short local rewording preserves every substantive claim and guarantee; no new argument is needed.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: The universal approximation capability of H\'enonNets implies that any symplectic diffeomorphism, including the nonlinear embedding defined above, can be approximated arbitrarily closely by composing a fixed linear embedding with H\'enonNet transformations.

issues.failure_explanation: Theorem thm:universal-approx is stated with no proof anywhere in the source. Its only justification is the prose inference that because HenonNets densely approximate symplectic diffeomorphisms of R^{2n}, they can approximate symplectic embeddings Phi: R^{2k} -> R^{2n} (k < n). This inference is invalid: a dimension-raising symplectic embedding is not a symplectic diffeomorphism of R^{2n}, so the cited density theorem does not apply to it. Establishing the theorem requires a nontrivial missing step, namely extending Phi composed with the inclusion to a global symplectomorphism of R^{2n} (Weinstein's symplectic neighborhood theorem plus compactly supported isotopy extension) before the HenonNet density result can be invoked.

failure_location.quote: This composite structure possesses universal approximation capability for symplectic embeddings, as formalized in the following theorem:

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Supply the missing contained argument: extend Phi (defined near the compact domain) via the Weinstein symplectic neighborhood theorem to a compactly supported symplectomorphism Psi of R^{2n} with Psi restricted to the image of iota equal to the embedding, then approximate Psi composed with the inverse linear factor by a HenonNet/G-reflector composite using the cited density results.
issues.overall_effect: The paper's central structural guarantee for the composite embedding (exact symplecticity plus approximation of arbitrary symplectic embeddings) is unestablished, as are the surrounding prose claims of 'practical equivalence due to universal approximation' in Section 3.2.
issues.title: Universal approximation theorem for symplectic embeddings is asserted with no valid supporting argument
issues.why_classification: The repair is a contained but genuinely nontrivial new lemma (symplectic extension); the advertised approximation guarantee survives in comparable form, so the issue is more than minor but avoids major loss.

issues.failure_explanation: For omega^2 = 0.01 the wave speed is omega = 0.1, so u(1,t) = h(a0|1/2 - x0 - omega t|), which equals h(0) = 1 at t = 10(1/2 - x0) in [3, 7] and is nonzero on an O(1) subinterval of the simulated/training horizon [0,12] for every sampled (a0, x0). Hence u(x,t) = u^0(x - omega t), which satisfies the PDE and initial conditions, does not satisfy the imposed Dirichlet conditions u(0,t) = u(1,t) = 0 on the simulated interval; the solution of the stated IBVP contains a boundary reflection (which the Dirichlet stencil D_xx in eq:D_xx produces) that the displayed closed form omits. The displayed 'exact solution' is therefore not a solution of the stated initial-boundary-value problem on the simulated time interval.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict the closed-form solution to times before the wavefront reaches x = 1 (t < 10(1/2 - x0 - 2/a0)), or restate the boundary conditions (e.g., periodic) consistently with the traveling-wave solution; a local correction and every numerical claim survives.
issues.overall_effect: The reference 'Exact' data of Example 1 (generated from the Dirichlet semi-discrete system) contain reflected waves, so the stated closed-form solution and the framing of the reconstruction-accuracy claims for Example 1 are unreliable as written.
issues.title: Example 1's claimed exact solution violates its own Dirichlet boundary conditions
issues.why_classification: A local reformulation of the example's statement suffices; the ROM methodology, rates, and advertised scope are unaffected.

issues.failure_explanation: With the displayed Hamiltonian, grad_p H = Delta x * p, so J_{2N} grad_z H = (Delta x * p, Delta x * omega^2 D_xx q) (up to boundary terms), whereas for the displayed L = diag(I_N, omega^2 D_xx), J_{2N} L z = (omega^2 D_xx q, -q). The two displayed expressions are unequal, so the chain of equalities is false. Moreover, J L z yields q_ddot = -omega^2 D_xx q (exponentially growing modes), not the wave equation q_dd = omega^2 q_xx that the example intends; the correct formulation requires L = diag(-omega^2 D_xx, I_N) with an unweighted energy. Additionally, the displayed H assigns half weight to every nearest-neighbor edge, which double-counts interior edges and under-weights the two boundary edges relative to -(1/2) q^T D_xx q, so grad_q H does not match -Delta x * omega^2 D_xx q at the boundary nodes.

failure_location.quote: \frac{d}{d t} \mathbf{z}=\bbJ_{2 N} \nabla_{\bf z} H({\bf z})=\bbJ_{2 N} L \, \mathbf{z}

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the displayed energy by the unweighted discrete energy H = (1/2) sum p_i^2 + (omega^2/(2 Delta x^2)) sum (q_{i+1}-q_i)^2 (so grad H = (-omega^2 D_xx q, p) = L z with L = diag(-omega^2 D_xx, I_N)); a local rewrite, all downstream experiments unchanged.
issues.overall_effect: The semi-discrete model stated as the basis of Example 1 (and from which the reference Störmer–Verlet data and the monitored Hamiltonian are described) is not the finite-difference discretization of the wave equation; the displayed formulation is false.
issues.title: Example 1's displayed semi-discrete Hamiltonian identity is internally inconsistent

issues.failure_explanation: With the canonical ordering z = (q, p) used throughout the paper, the flow of the displayed H_cont gives q_t = delta H/delta p = -2 p_xx + 2*epsilon*(q^2+p^2) p, which is not the stated equation q_t = p_xx + epsilon*(q^2+p^2) p of eq:schro-can (the sign of the quadratic part is flipped and the nonlinear coefficient is doubled). The Hamiltonian that generates eq:schro-can is -1/2*Int(q_x^2 + p_x^2)dx + (epsilon/4)*Int(q^2+p^2)^2 dx; the displayed H_cont is neither this nor its negative, and in particular is not conserved by eq:schro-can (it equals the conserved energy plus a non-conserved multiple of the L^4 mass with the wrong sign structure).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Display the flow-generating energy H_cont = -1/2 Int (q_x^2 + p_x^2) dx + (epsilon/4) Int (q^2+p^2)^2 dx (consistent with the (q,p) = (Im u, Re u) splitting and the semi-discrete system), or flip the sign convention of the PDE; a local formula correction.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: \frac{d}{d t} \mathbf{z}=\bbJ_{2 N} \nabla_{\bf z} H({\bf z})=\bbJ_{2 N} L\mathbf{z} + \bbJ_{2 N}\mathbf{g}(\bf z),

issues.failure_explanation: For the displayed identity dz/dt = J_{2N} grad_z H = J_{2N} L z + J_{2N} g(z) to hold, grad_z H must equal L z + g(z); with L = diag(D_xx, D_xx) this requires the quadratic terms (1/2) q^T D_xx q + (1/2) p^T D_xx p, i.e., negatively signed second differences ((q_{i+1}-q_i)^2 terms), plus the quartic potential (Delta x * epsilon/4) Sum (q_i^2+p_i^2)^2. The displayed Hamiltonian instead contains positively signed quartic difference terms (q_{i-1}q_i - q_i^2)^2/Delta x^2 = q_i^2 (q_{i-1}-q_i)^2 / Delta x^2 and only a quadratic potential (epsilon/4)(p_i^2+q_i^2) (missing the square). Hence grad_z H differs from L z + g(z) (e.g., the displayed derivative contributions are cubic in z rather than the required linear D_xx z plus the cubic g), so the displayed Hamiltonian does not generate the displayed semi-discrete system; the accompanying display of g(z) also omits the factor epsilon present in eq:schro-can.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the discrete energy by the one consistent with L = diag(D_xx, D_xx) and g, namely H = (Delta x/2)(q^T D_xx q + p^T D_xx p) + (Delta x * epsilon/4) Sum (q_i^2+p_i^2)^2 (with a consistent overall normalization), and restore the factor epsilon in g(z); a local formula correction.
issues.overall_effect: The discrete Hamiltonian reported in eq:schro-ham-discre, used for the Hamiltonian-conservation assessment of Example 3 (Figure schro-ham and the prose claiming preservation 'on the order of machine precision'), does not correspond to the stated semi-discrete Hamiltonian system.
